quest.title: I, Flame Bearer
quest.description: Following your deal with Kinich, you prepare to walk around the tribe, making room for him to maneuver...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Walk around the tribe the next day (08:00 - 12:00)
Talk to Huni and Toba

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Huni! How can you call the Mountain King a monster?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Because he hurt a lot of people! And look what happened to Nanna...

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: But it wasn't on purpose! The Mountain King is sick, that's all. He's been hurt by the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: That's true, but the fact remains that he's now a threat to all of us!

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: How can you be so harsh to someone who's sick? If you don't take back what you just said, I don't know if we can carry on being friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Toba... Huni... What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Huni's saying nasty things about the Mountain King! It's not right, he's our hero!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Hmph, once upon a time, maybe. But not anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey now, let's not fight. Aren't you best friends?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Hmph, yesterday, maybe. But not anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Toba! Fine... I guess my dad is right. Things change, and you just have to accept it and move forward.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: As of today, our friendship is over! There's no going back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh come on, cut it out you two! We have some great news to tell you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} is gonna be the flame bearer for the next Turnfire Night! {M#He}{F#She}'s gonna do a beautiful ceremony and cure the Mountain King's illness for good.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: What? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Of course. I'm an expert at this stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: So that's what my dad wanted to talk to you about?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: To be fair, from what we saw the other day, you are pretty good at climbing cliffs. Probably just as good as Kinich.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Wait, speaking of Kinich... Where even is that guy?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, good question... Is he not coming to the ceremony anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can get him to come. But if he catches you two fighting again, he won't be happy! He'll be sure to give you both a piece of his mind!

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: No, we can't let that happen! I've never even spoken to him before! I can't afford to make such a bad first impression.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: I didn't mean to argue with Toba... All I said was that the Mountain King has done some pretty bad things. He was the one who turned it into a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You two clearly care about each other. The Mountain King can't change that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! If you weren't friends, there's no way Toba would've come to look for the baby Saurians with you.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: #...Alright, well... Because it's {NICKNAME} and Paimon, and Kinich... I'm sorry, Toba. I'm sorry for all the mean things I said about the Mountain King.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Dad just really misses Nanna. And I was really upset that she's gone, too...

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: #I shouldn't have spoken to you the way I did either. It wasn't very nice of me. For {NICKNAME} and Paimon, Kinich, and for Nanna... I'm sorry too, Huni.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's more like it... Now you're best friends again!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Guess so... Toba, if I ever say something mean about the Mountain King in the future, I'll make sure I say it to someone else and not you.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: I'd better go buy some colored cloth for my Dad now. He needs it for Turnfire Night. Let's play again some other time.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: #See you, Toba. See you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Kay, I'll head home as well then... See you next time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, take care you two...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww... Even though they said they're sorry, it looks like their friendship isn't as strong as it was before.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Times really are changing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...Let's just hope we can solve this once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, let's move on.

talks.objective: Continue walking around the tribe

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, what's happening here?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: A rehearsal, for the Turnfire Night dance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oooh! There's a dance involved? Paimon wants to learn, too...

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: You don't know it? Ah, I guess you're not from these parts, huh? It's rare to see a new face around the tribe these days — I thought everyone would be keeping away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why do you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Because of the Turnfire Night, of course. The Mountain King could wake up at any time — that's why we're holding an emergency ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: This isn't one of those fun-and-games festivals. For outsiders, it might even be a little dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, did you know that the flame bearer this time is actually gonna be an outsider?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Oh, I did hear about that! It's a first for sure. I would've loved to meet them in person.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Heh... Now you have.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: What? Oh...! It's you!? Man, oh man... Well, this is a nice surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: It's funny, I was just thinking that I'll probably miss out on meeting the new flame bearer, since I'm not taking part this time around... Then suddenly, there you are! Must be my lucky day, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're not taking part in Turnfire Night? How come? You're not an outsider too, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Haha, you must be joking! Watch this...

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Not bad, right? Yeah, I'm considered one of the better-looking guys who dances beneath the Pillars of the Sacred Flame. Been doing it a few years. Always gets the ladies out to watch, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, very impressive! So why did you quit?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Well, I feel like the whole Mountain King situation is getting more and more precarious. It's just not safe here anymore. One of our elders' Saurian companions even lost her life not long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: The question is, what are we going to do about this in the long term? But our leaders don't have any answers for us. They're probably too busy fighting about it amongst themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: The way things are going, it's only a matter of time before it gets violent. So I figured, y'know what? Now's as good a time as any to get away for little while, go do some exploring.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You look a little disappointed...

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Disappointed? Nah. It's a great opportunity to go see the world. As every male Scion of the Canopy knows: Wherever you are and wherever you go, the only way is forwards. We take pride in that. I won't forget my roots.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fair enough. So what's your plan for the next step?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Hehe, I managed to get in touch with the Saurian Relics Association. They gave me a simple test: Find a decent quality relic, and they'll make me a member.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the Saurian Relics Association?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: You've never heard of it? It's a group of amateur history enthusiasts who do research on the ancient Saurian era. They're all about collecting relics and remnants from that age.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, the guy who was flame bearer before you — I've heard that his Saurian buddy comes from that time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ajaw? Ajaw's a relic from an ancient Saurian civilization!?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Oh! Yeah, him. So you know those two already, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Then do you know how they met? It was deep inside some mysterious ruin, and they signed a contract there. The association folks say that kind of contract usually comes with a huge, hidden cost.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? That sounds ominous...

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Who knows? But if it's true, Kinich can probably handle it. He knows what he's doing with weighing up contracts and costs and stuff. I doubt he'd make a contract that doesn't benefit him.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Strangely enough, I actually happened upon a strange mural a while back, and it looked to me like it was depicting a Saurian and a human involved in some kind of Saurian-era contract ritual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, does that count as a relic then?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: You bet it does. I was all ready to go take a picture of it and use that as my entry ticket to the association.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: But after all the Abyssal activity recently, I heard that area's been overrun by monsters. The best laid plans, huh? I'll just have to wait and see if things improve.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: ...Or... You look like you know your way around a fight... I don't suppose there's any chance you'd be able to help...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If all you need is to get a picture, that should be pretty achievable, right...? {NICKNAME} deals with monsters all the time, it's a piece of cake.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Wait, you're seriously gonna help me out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, it's no big deal! Compared to some of the things we've been roped into before, this is nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: ...Pyro Archon above, you two have hearts of gold, you know that? You're the kind of people who could dive into the Turnfire, deep in the bowels of the Night Kingdom, and it wouldn't burn a single hair off your head.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll take that as a... compliment?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Of course it is! Alright, come with me, I'll show you the way!

talks.objective: Go to the location of the mural indicated by Thiago

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: There it is, it's inside these ruins. As you can see, the place is crawling with monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alrighty then. Stay back and take cover, Thiago — this could get dangerous. We'll take care of them.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Great minds think alike, haha! I'm not about to cramp your style.

talks.objective: Fend off the monsters
Examine the mural

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, that should be the last of them... It's a good thing Thiago had the sense to stay in his hiding place, or things could've gotten really hairy for him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look! That's gotta be it, right? Definitely looks like a mural.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a little on the small side...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, true... Now that you mention it, most ancient murals take up a whole huge wall. This looks more like someone with a paintbrush got bored and started doodling...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It does match the story he told us, though. There's a Saurian and a human... So is that supposed to be what an ancient contract ritual looked like...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, whatever, we're not here to decipher it, just photograph it.

talks.objective: Take a picture of the mural
Return to where Thiago is

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: You've been robbed!? Oh, Ponche... And I thought my luck was bad.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I put blood, sweat, and tears into that! And now I've got nothing to show for it. Some gap-toothed goon stole it from me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thiago! Is this the picture you were looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Let me take a look... Yep, that's the one! Pyro Archon above, you two are superhumans!

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Hey, Ponche, come and say hi to these guys. They're gonna be the new flame bearers, and they're tough as nails.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: #Wait, are you... {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Huh? You already know each other?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Don't think so...?

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: My nephew, Toba's been telling everyone about you. He says you're crazy strong, super friendly, that you helped him out, and that you're going to be our flame bearers this Turnfire Night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, so you're Toba's uncle! Great to meet you, Sir!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like we've managed to make a bit of a name for ourselves, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Toba's not wrong, my friend. These two are honestly some of the nicest, most genuine people I've ever met. Everyone speaks incredibly highly of them. Seriously, if you're comfortable telling them about what happened, I guarantee you they'll sort it out in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Really? All I want is to get the fruits of my labor back...

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Allow me to explain. Ponche is a well-known scholar within our tribe, author of the widely acclaimed book, "Yupanqui's Turnfire." Unfortunately, the book was stolen by a Treasure Hoarder a few hours ago.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I spent years of my life researching that book... I visited every last ruin, interviewed every descendant of every hero in our history...

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: On the word "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo" alone, I covered at least five different interpretations of the meaning, based on accounts from different villages.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: It was an unparalleled masterpiece!

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: And now it's all gone. That little goon ambushed me during my morning walk. He snatched all of my belongings, including my entire manuscript!

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: That book was everything to him... it's like they robbed him of his soul when they took it. Look at him, lost and listless... He's a shell of the man he was.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Dear honored guests of our clan... I am but a helpless old student. If only for Toba and Thiago's sake, please help me, I beg of you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where were you ambushed?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: See what I mean, Ponche? Now you've run into these two, your luck's about to change, big time.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I don't know if he's still there, but... Come on, I'll take you!

talks.objective: Help Ponche recover the stolen book

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Hey! You... you thieving rat! Give me my things back!

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: What do you want now, you old bum? God, you're a waste of space. Prepare to get shoved butt-first into a tree hollow!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I dare you to try.

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: Aw, what's this? Brought a little bodyguard with you, huh? Alright, let's see what you've got... Watch this!

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: Eat dirt, suckers!

talks.objective: Catch up to "Eight-Hands" Matthias

dialogues.speaker: Ponini
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Poggi
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Pocchi
dialogues.text: Grrr...

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: Where did these yumkasaurs come from? Get away from me, you monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! The baby Saurians are blocking his path!

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: Stop, please! By all the warriors, heroes, gods, and kings... I can't run any longer.

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: Please, I don't have your stuff anymore... Have mercy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah? Well, where is it then?

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: I... threw it away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You threw it away!?

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: The old bum's bag didn't have a single Mora in it. Just a tatty old book, worn-out pens, and some old rags.

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: All that time lying in wait was for nothing. I was so mad, I just threw all of it away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Is that really the truth? Okay then, where did you throw it away?

dialogues.speaker: Matthias
dialogues.text: Same place you found me... I swear on the Pyro Archon, it's the truth! May all my worldly possessions be turned to ash by Turnfire if I'm lying!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, that's a pretty strong oath...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do now? It sounds like he's telling the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go back to where we were and see if we can find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right... Let's hope nobody gets to the book before we do... We'll never get it back then...

talks.objective: Interrogate him about the location of the book

talks.objective: Interrogate him about the location of the book
In a hidden cave...

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: "...Although the Turnfire is a heroic symbol in Huitztlan, it also comes with the more ominous implication of eventual tragedy..."

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: "...This holds true for all bearers of this ancient name in recorded history. Each one of them died of non-natural causes, as if the specter of the Turnfire was always lurking in the background..."

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: "...This appears to suggest the existence of some higher power that is always watching the name-bearer, examining their actions and eventually demanding payment in return. None can escape this payment — unless, perhaps, they could honestly swear by Turnfire to never make a single mistake in their entire life..."

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: "Yupanqui's Turnfire"... What an incredible work on ancient name philology. I can't believe it was just lying there for me to take.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Let me see, the author is... Ponche. Nice. A gentleman and a scholar.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Silence, book muncher! The Great K'uhul Ajaw will suffer your droning voice no longer!

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Do you truly find no joy at all in perusing such rich historical records?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Joy? What joy is there in this pointless drivel?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Well, it makes a pretty shocking prediction: Every bearer of the ancient name "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo" eventually meets a grisly end. Maybe that's the price you pay for the name that means "price"?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: What? You're saying, Kinich will die a violent death? ...Mwuhahaha! So I'll finally get to take over his body?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: When? When will that glorious day arrive? The Great K'uhul Ajaw demands to know!

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Wow, you are just irredeemable, aren't you? An agent of chaos down to the core. You make us Abyss Order folks look like saints in comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Silence, maggot! To presume that anyone compares your kind with the Great K'uhul Ajaw is sheer vanity! And if that day ever comes, your doom will soon follow.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Hehe, you don't need to lecture me about doomsday. Here's what I know, based on countless historical texts:

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: All civilizations will be reduced to rubble by the passage of time. From ancient kingdoms, to heavenly thrones, to worlds beyond... There are no exceptions.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: But from the ruins of every civilization, the dust will rise and never settle, thus transcending the confines of time. That "dust" is what we call a civilization's spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: And you, Great K'uhul Ajaw, are one such speck of dust from a bygone age. I've paid dearly for the chance to observe you up close.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Now, let me take a good look at you. We'll see whether any memories of that age still remain inside you...

talks.objective: Return to the Scions of the Canopy

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're so sorry, Mr. Ponche... But we couldn't find your manuscript anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Does that mean... All of my hard work was for nothing...?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: You gotta stay positive, Ponche. You might've lost the book, but the brains behind it are still intact. Surely you remember the main points, at least?

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: The whole reason I worked so hard to get it finished before the Turnfire Night is because I hoped that maybe it might help us find a way through these trying times. But now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean... You solved the Mountain King problem?

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Well, not exactly. But I thought my research might at least be a starting point...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, really? So what did you find out in your research?

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I think the key to all of this lies in the power of "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo"...

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: ...Ponche, you know as well as anyone that ancient names don't hold any real power. Symbolic power doesn't count.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: You're right, but "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo" may be a special case. Given that it first arose in the era of the First Pyro Archon, it might contain remnants of Xbalanque's power.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Yeah, I remember that story — my grandpa told it to me when I was a little kid...

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Maybe you're the special case... Most kids stop believing in that stuff by your age...

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I'm not talking about childhood superstitions here! There is evidence!

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Like what?

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Like the fact that the Mountain King is still alive. Everyone attributes that to the power of the Abyss, but there's more to it than that.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: The key factor is that Burkina summoned the power of "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo," at the cost of his own life.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: If you don't believe me, then answer me this: How many other creatures can you think of who lived longer, not shorter, after being contaminated by the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Um... {NICKNAME}... Different situation, but similar idea: Doesn't this remind you of the hili—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shh!

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: So, I came to the conclusion that "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo" must refer to some mysterious ritual involving a tit-for-tat exchange.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: It began with the first Pyro Archon, fell with the Grand Alliance, then was buried in the Night Kingdom... And now, it awaits the call of its new bearer.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Hey, hey... Sorry to interrupt, Ponche, but you seem to be getting a little over-excited.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... I was originally planning on presenting my findings to Kinich. I'd hoped he would be attending the upcoming ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Sounds to me like you dreamed up one fanciful theory to support another.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Kinich, what are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I more or less finished what I was doing, so I came to have a quick catchup. Now a good time?

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Kinich! I'm onto something! I haven't worked out all the details, but, but... You have to attend the Turnfire Night!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... So Mr. Ponche here has done a lot of research on the history of the Turnfire, and thinks he might have found a way for you to solve the problem...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'll be there, Ponche.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Let's go.

talks.objective: Go off to the side and chat with Kinich

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Here will do.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you found a way to summon a Beastly Rift?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah. I'd like your help giving it a trial run tomorrow. If that works, we have our plan come Turnfire Night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you're not considering Ponche's idea...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You heard him — he hasn't worked out the details yet. We need a more practical solution with concrete steps to follow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Yet"... Are you saying, you think he might actually be onto something?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I think it's possible, based on something I know about the war five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Burkina didn't fall to the Abyss — he was killed by the Mountain King in an episode of madness. In his final moments, Burkina made the fateful decision not to fight back, and instead pass his blood and power onto the Mountain King.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Maybe he thought the Mountain King was stronger than him, and more valuable to the tribe. Or maybe it was just out of loyalty to his friend.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Either way, I can believe the Turnfire was involved. Whether you think his sacrifice triggered it, or his fate was sealed from the moment he took the Malipo name... It makes sense to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...How can you drop these truth-bombs with such a straight face...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: This is what I've gleaned from my many interactions with the Mountain King. His mind is so disordered, it took some time to piece it all together.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The story Elder Trinidad told you was the more palatable version of events. The truth is even darker.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The Mountain King's mind isn't just disordered. He is suffering, and feels great shame. I believe he wants to be put out of his misery.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Then... Then what should we do? Should we grant him his wish?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Of course not. We should help him move to a new home.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So your goal hasn't changed.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It's the only practical solution.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The Mountain King is a hero to my tribe — an object of worship, even. Ending his life would be like desecrating a statue.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Still, he's been the cause of multiple disasters, and we can't afford to have any more.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Practical solutions hurt Paimon's brain. Can we follow our hearts next time...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Haha, then let's break for the day. I've already found a suitable venue for tomorrow.

talks.objective: Wait till the next day (8:00 – 12:00)
Go and meet up with Kinich

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You're here. Very punctual.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Ohohoho! So, the gruesome twosome come crawling back... Here to make amends after the gross irreverence you displayed last time?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Very well! The Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw shall grant you the audience that you seek. Now pucker up, and kiss our feet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich, didn't you say you found him a teacher? He's just as out-of-control as ever!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: No one gets to discipline the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw! NO ONE!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you put up with this behavior?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Maybe because I've never had a gentle-natured companion like Paimon to compare against.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I—Is that a compliment?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah. I see what I'm missing out on now. And it's a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Kiniiiiiich! We could drown this measly flying ant in one droplet of spit! How dare you compare her to the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Just wait till I possess your dead body! I will commit heinous atrocities! Tear down your legacy! Destroy your reputation! Wreak havoc on your—

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's get down to business. Once we've opened the Beastly Rift, you're welcome to toss Ajaw in there for a couple days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: With pleasure! You don't need to ask twice!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Check it out, I got my hands on this device in a trade. It's meant as bait, but it'll also stabilize the Abyssal energy.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The Rifthounds will tear through space to get to this. Once they're here, we take them out and claim the rift for ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did you get your hands on this?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You'll find out soon enough. First, let's try this out.

talks.objective: Clear the Rifthounds out

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: This is far back enough, right? I'm not in the way or anything?

talks.objective: Talk to the thing calling itself "Sanka"

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After you clear the wave of Rifthounds, a more powerful burst of Abyssal energy ripples through the Rift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh... Are there even bigger ones on the way?
You see, Kinich? I'm a man of my word. In fact, I'd say I under-promised and over-delivered. Nifty little gizmo, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I take it this is your true form.
Now that our deal is complete, it's time to start the next phase of our relationship. I made a promise to the Great K'uhul Ajaw, and now I'm here to seize your body for his use.
Cliché, I know — the hero's trusted partner sells him out to the Abyss in a shocking act of betrayal. Cue bad-guy speech and drawn-out death sequence...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Enjou!?
Huh...? HUH!? What are you two doing here? Oh, Mr. Kinich, this is not what we agreed on.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, this is the gift I got you. I know you're looking for intel on the Abyss Order, so I thought he might be of use to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But it looks like you've already met?

response.text: Yikes, frosty reception... Gotta say, I kinda pictured this moment going a little differently. Tears of joy welling up in your eyes as you say the words: "It's good to see you again, old friend."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be ridiculous... Sounds like you've been reading too many romance novels.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: There we have it. Change is inevitable, and nothing lasts forever. What a pity... Well then, time for you to meet the new me. This time, please call me Sanka.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sanka! Aha, so YOU'RE glasses guy! You tricked Huni and Toba into telling you a bunch of stories!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's your real name?

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: What does it matter? A name is a superficial label, it's what's deep down inside that counts. And I've shown you the deepest parts of me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You mean the masochistic parts?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That would explain a lot. Why else would you show up here and start acting like a wise guy? You looking for a fight?

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: Eh, I'll pass. I do rather like you, as I've said before, but my one quibble is that you really don't know your own strength.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then what are you doing here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... Of course! You're the one behind all the recent Abyss activity! Let Paimon guess, you've been provoking the Mountain King, too?

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: Haven't I told you before? I'm not part of the inner circle who do our Highness's bidding. My interests are far more low-stakes.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: I spend my time digging for truth in ancient doodads and books. You really think a benchwarmer like me is capable of more than that?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I investigated him — he's not connected to the recent events. Just happens to be in the area.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: So I struck a deal with him: He helps me summon a Rift, I allow him to do some "historical research."

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: But that's all over, and now Kinich wants to hand me over to you, while I was hoping this would be an opportune moment to whisk away his body.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: That would've given me some more time to study the Great K'uhul Ajaw.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: But now I've run into you, which is just my luck... Or maybe I've incited the wrath of the Turnfire, and this is the price I have to pay. But I don't understand, what did I do wrong?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You tricked Huni and Toba.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: Wait, does that count? Hmm, let me think...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ajaw, you are the worst of the worst! Colluding with the Abyss Order against Kinich? How could you betray your partner?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: There is no betrayal! The Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw is a partner to no one.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Don't worry, I told him to act as bait.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Yes, and you should have picked a bigger fish! The Abyss Order? What a joke! Not even a match for our lowly servant. I put up with this toad's croaking for days, and it was all for nothing!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: It looks like your disciplinary measures have been less than effective, Mr. Enjou.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: Eh, what did you expect? Behavioral rehab isn't really our thing. Otherwise, we might as well change our name from the Abyss Order to the Abyss Boarding School.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: The Abysmal Disorder would suit you better. Kinich! Dispose of him! He is of no further use to us.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: #{NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Be my guest. The Abyss Order is a threat to us all.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: Hey now, I may be a lowly clerk, but don't underestimate me.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: I could never beat you in a straight-up fight, but when it comes to running away, I won't lose to anyone.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: Do me a favor and remember how fast I disappear. Maybe then you'll show me a little respect next time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Darn, he got away again... Couldn't you have stopped him?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: It's alright, he's not worth our time and energy. Besides, it seems like he's in debt to a lot of people — I'm sure they'll keep him busy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, if you say so... Still, Paimon's kinda surprised that you actually struck a deal with someone from the Abyss Order.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: To borrow that guy's words, names are superficial labels. Whether you call it the Abyss Order or anything else, it's a broad generalization at best.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Think of it like apples that have fallen from a tree. If you tasted each one, you'd find that they're all at different stages of ripening.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Even the unripe fruit blown off its branch before it's fully grown can still be brewed into a fine wine. Everything has its use.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Well, in that specific sense, maybe Enjou's not such a bad apple. Not rotten to the core, at least.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Of course! Only the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw is rotten to the core, and evil beyond redemption!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... So what exactly are you, anyway? You're definitely the evilest little thing Paimon's ever met.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Don't worry, he can't hurt a fly.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Because you signed a contract?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: You could say that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Paimon heard that those kinds of contracts might come with a terrible cost attached... I—Is that true?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Such as? Ajaw watching me like a ravenous vulture?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Vulture? Vulture!? We are the dragon supreme! Sovereign ruler of the Nation of Flame!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Let's pick this up another time. It's getting kinda late.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: You should go back and get some rest. Big day ahead — tomorrow's Turnfire Night. Time to light the sacred flame and burn away the filth for a legendary five-hundred-year-old warrior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah... Hearing you lay it out like that is making Paimon a little nervous. For all the work we've put in, it all comes down to tomorrow night. We have to make sure we solve this problem once and for all.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Then it can't hurt to say this one more time: Good luck to us both.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Good luck to us both.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: See you tomorrow.

choices.text: Let him go. He'll never amount to much in the Abyss Order anyway.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Sanka"
response.text: You see, this is why I like you. Still, you shouldn't underestimate me just because I'm a lowly clerk.

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, in a hidden cave...
